He said: "He is under the influence of a spell (tubba)." He asked: "And what is tubba?" He said: "He has been bewitched (suhira)." He asked: "Who bewitched him?" He said: "Labid ibn A'sam, the Jew." He asked: "With what did he bewitch him?" He said: "With a comb and combings." He asked: "And where is it?" He said: "In a sheath of a date-palm spathe, under a rā'ūfa in the well of Dharwan." Al-Juff is the skin of the date-palm spathe, and al-Rā'ūfa is a protruding rock at the bottom of the well on which the one drawing water stands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up alarmed and said: "O 'Aishah, did you not realise that Allah has informed me of my illness?" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Ali, al-Zubayr and 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and they drained the water of the well until it looked like the soaking water of henna. Then they lifted the rock and took out the sheath, and in it were the combings of his head and teeth from his comb, and in it was a cord tied with twelve knots, stuck with needles. So Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, and every time he recited a verse, a knot came undone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt relief when the last knot was undone, and he stood up as if he had been released from a tether. Jibril, peace be upon him, began saying: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from an envier and an evil eye; may Allah cure you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take out the wicked man and kill him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for me, Allah has cured me, and I dislike that evil should be stirred up among the people." [[Al-Kashf wal-Bayan of al-Tha'labi (fol. 194, Mahmudiyya edition).]]

He cited it thus without an isnad, and in it there is strangeness, and in some of it there is severe objectionability, while parts of it have supporting evidence from what has preceded. And Allah knows best.

**Tafsir of the Two Surahs of Seeking Refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn)**

They are both Madani (revealed in Medina).

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Asim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Ibn Mas'ud [was] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] not writing the two Mu'awwidhat in his mushaf?" He said: "I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me that Jibril, peace be upon him, said to him: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak (﴿Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi al-falaq﴾).' So I said it. He said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind (﴿Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi an-nas﴾).' So I said it." So we say what the Prophet ﷺ said. [[Al-Musnad (5/129).]]

Abu Bakr al-Humaydi also narrated it in his Musnad, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah and Asim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, that they both heard Zirr ibn Hubaysh say: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b about the two Mu'awwidhat, and I said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud erases them from the mushaf." He said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'It was said to me: Say, so I said.'" So we say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. [[Musnad al-Humaydi (1/185).]]

Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about the two Mu'awwidhat, and he said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about them, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said it to you. So say it.'" My father said: "Then the Prophet ﷺ said to us..." So we say [it]. [[Al-Musnad (5/129).]]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, and Asim narrated to us from Zirr, who said: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b and said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud says such and such." He said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said.'" So we say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4977).]]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i, from Qutaybah, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Abdah and Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4976).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Azraq ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Salt ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, who said: "'Abd Allah used to erase the two Mu'awwidhat from the mushaf and say: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was only commanded to seek refuge with them, and 'Abd Allah did not recite with them.'" [[Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, no. (2301), via Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub, from Hassan ibn Ibrahim, and al-Bazzar said: "No one among the Companions followed 'Abd Allah in this. It is authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ that he recited them in prayer, and we have affirmed them in the mushaf."]]

'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: "'Abd Allah used to erase the two Mu'awwidhat from his mushafs and say: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'" [[In the original: "from 'Abd Allah." The text reads "'Abd al-Rahman".]] Al-A'mash said: Asim narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked us about them, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said.'" [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/129).]]

This is well known among many of the reciters and jurists: that Ibn Mas'ud did not write the two Mu'awwidhat in his mushaf. Perhaps he had not heard them from the Prophet ﷺ, and they had not reached him through mass transmission (tawatur). Then perhaps he later returned from that view to the position of the majority, for the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wrote them in the leading mushafs, and sent them to all the regions in that form. And to Allah belongs all praise and favour.

Muslim said in his Sahih: Qutaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Have you not seen verses that were revealed tonight, the like of which has never been seen: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind'?" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (814).]]

Ahmad, Muslim also, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Uqbah, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/144); Sahih Muslim, no. (814); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2902); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/158).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Ibn Jabir narrated to us, from al-Qasim Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: "While I was leading the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the reins on one of those mountain paths, he said to me: 'O 'Uqbah, will you not ride?'" He said: "I was too modest to ride his mount, so he said: 'O 'Uqbah, will you not ride?'" He said: [Addition from the Musnad.] "I feared it might be disobedience. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted, and I rode for a short while, then he rode. Then he said: 'O 'Uqbah, shall I not teach you two surahs, among the best two surahs that people have recited?'" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he taught me: "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak" and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind." Then the prayer was established, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went forward and recited them in it. Then he passed by me and said: "How did you find them, O 'Uqbah? Recite them whenever you sleep and whenever you rise." [[In the original: "O 'Uqab"; the marginal note reads "O 'Uqb". Addition from the Musnad.]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, both from Ibn Jabir, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/144); Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/253).]]

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Harith, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Uqbah, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252-253); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1462).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Yazid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Ru'ayni and Abu Marhum narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from 'Ali ibn Rabah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the Mu'awwidhat (al-mu'awwidhat) at the end of every prayer.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several routes, from 'Ali ibn Abi Rabah. [[Al-Musnad (4/155); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1523); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2903); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/68).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib."

Another route: Ahmad said: Yahya [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "Muhammad".]] ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Mashrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Recite the two Mu'awwidhat, for you will never recite the like of them." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was presented with a white mule, and he mounted it, and 'Uqbah took its reins to lead it for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Uqbah".]] said: "Recite: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.'" So he repeated it for him until he had recited it. He noticed that I was not very pleased with it, so he said: "Perhaps you were careless about it? For you have never stood in prayer reciting anything like it."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Baqiyyah, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/149); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7843-7844).]] Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the two Mu'awwidhat, and he related something similar. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, I heard al-Nu'man, from Ziyad Abi al-Asad, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "People have never sought refuge with the like of these two: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7856).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Abu 'Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "O 'Uqbah, say." I said: "What shall I say?" He was silent with me, then he said: "Say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He was silent with me. So I said: "O Allah, return it to me." He said: "O 'Uqbah, say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,'" and I recited it until I reached its end. Then he said: "Say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind,'" and I recited it until I reached its end. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point: "No one has asked with the like of these two, nor has anyone sought refuge with the like of these two." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/253).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Yasar informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Harith, from Makhul, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited them both in the Fajr prayer. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu 'Imran Aslam, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I followed [[In the manuscript M: "I came to".]] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was riding, so I placed my hands on his foot [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "on his feet".]] and said: "Teach me Surah Hud or Surah Yusuf." He said: "You will not recite anything more beneficial [[In the manuscript M: "more effective".]] in the sight of Allah than: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/254).]]

Another hadith: al-Nasa'i said: Mahmud ibn Khalid informed us, al-Walid narrated to us, Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'A'ish [[In the manuscript A: "Ibn 'Abbas".]] al-Juhani, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "O son of 'A'ish, shall I not show you, or inform you, of the best that those who seek refuge can seek refuge with?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind'; these are the two surahs." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/251).]]

Thus these routes from 'Uqbah are, as a body, like mutawatir reports from him, which give certainty according to many of the verifying scholars of hadith.

It has already been mentioned in the narration of Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan and Farwah ibn Mujahid, from him: "Shall I not teach you three surahs, the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan [[In the manuscript A: "in the Qur'an".]]? 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (﴿Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad﴾), 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'"

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu al-'Ala', who said: A man said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the people were taking turns riding, and the mounts on the back were few. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ's turn came, and then mine. He caught up with me and struck my shoulders [[Addition from the Musnad.]] and said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it, and I recited it with him. Then he said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it, and I recited it with him. Then he said: 'When you pray, recite them both.'" [[Al-Musnad (5/24).]]

It appears that this man was 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and Allah knows best.

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7859).]]

**Another hadith:** Al-Nasa'i said: Amr ibn Ali Abu Hafs informed us: Badal narrated to us: Shaddad ibn Sa'id Abu Talha narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, who narrated to us, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite, O Jabir." I said: "What should I recite, may my father and mother be your ransom?" He said: "Recite: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'" So I recited them, and he said: "Recite with them, for you will never recite the like of them." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7854.]

**Another hadith:** Al-Nasa'i said: Amr ibn Ali Abu Hafs informed us... [as above chain].

The hadith of Aisha has already passed, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recite them (the two surahs) and blow into his palms, then wipe with them his head, his face, and whatever part of his body he could reach.

Imam Malik said: From Ibn Shihab, from Urwa, from Aisha: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he was ill, would recite over himself the two Mu'awwidhatain (the two surahs of seeking refuge) and blow. When his pain grew severe, I would recite over him and wipe with his hand over him, seeking its blessing.

This was narrated by al-Bukhari from Abdullah ibn Yusuf, Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, al-Nasa'i from Qutayba and from the narrations of Ibn al-Qasim and Isa ibn Yunus, and Ibn Majah from the narrations of Ma'n and Bishr ibn Umar. All eight narrated it from Malik, with this wording. [Muwatta' 2/942; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5016; Sahih Muslim no. 3902; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3902; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra nos. 7549, 7544, 10847; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3529.]

It has already passed at the end of the surah "Nun" (Surah al-Qalam), from the hadith of Abu Nadra, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eye of jinn and humans. When the two Mu'awwidhatain were revealed, he took them and abandoned whatever else. This was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi said: it is a hasan (sound-good) hadith.

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful**

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Isam narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Hasan ibn Salih narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: "al-falaq" is the dawn.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is the dawn. It was also narrated from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, al-Hasan, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd, and Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam, the same as this.

Al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir said: it is like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿the Cleaver of the daybreak﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

Ali ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is the creation. Likewise al-Dahhak said: Allah commanded His Prophet to seek refuge from all of creation.

Ka'b al-Ahbar (ka'b al-Ahbar) said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is a house in Hell; when it is opened, all the people of the Fire cry out because of its intense heat. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this, then said:

My father narrated to us: Suhayl ibn Uthman narrated to us, from a man he named, from al-Suddi, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, that they said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is a pit at the bottom of Hell, covered by a lid. When it is uncovered, a fire emerges from it, and Hell cries out because of the intense heat of what comes out of it.

Similarly it was narrated from Amr ibn Abasa and al-Suddi and others. A marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith has come on this, but it is munkar (rejected). Ibn Jarir said:

Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti narrated to me: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan al-Wasiti narrated to us: Nasr ibn Khuzayma al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell." [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/225.] Its isnad is gharib (unusual), and its raising to the Prophet is not authentic.

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is one of the names of Hell.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the first, that it is the cleaving of the dawn. This is the sound view, and it is the choice of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Sahih. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/225; Sahih al-Bukhari 8/741, Fath.]

* *

His words: ﴿from the evil of what He created﴾ mean: from the evil of all created beings. Thabit al-Bunani and al-Hasan al-Basri said: Hell, Iblis and his offspring are among what He created.

﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾. Mujahid said: "al-ghasiq" is the night, "when it settles" means the setting of the sun. Al-Bukhari reported this from him, and Ibn Abi Najih narrated it from him. Likewise Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, Khusayf, al-Hasan and Qatada said: it is the night when it approaches with its darkness.

Al-Zuhri said: "when it settles" refers to the sun when it sets. From Atiyya and Qatada: "when the night settles" means when it departs. Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayra, said: "al-ghasiq" is a star. Ibn Zayd said: the Arabs used to say that "al-ghasiq" is the setting of the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), and diseases and plagues would increase when it set, and would lift when it rose.

Ibn Jarir said: For these views there is a report that Nasr ibn Ali narrated to me: Bakkar ibn Abdullah, the nephew of Hammam, narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: 'the star al-ghasiq.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/227.]

I say: This hadith is not authentic in its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: it is the moon.

I say: The main evidence of the proponents of this view is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Harith, from Abu Salama, who said: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand, showed me the moon as it rose, and said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this darkness when it settles."

It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the books of tafsir of their Sunan, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from his maternal uncle al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, with the same. al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. The wording is: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles." The wording of al-Nasa'i is: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, this is the darkness when it settles." [Musnad 6/61; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3366; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10138.]

The proponents of the first view, that it is the night when it comes in, said: This does not contradict our view, because the moon is a sign of the night, its authority exists only in it, and likewise the stars shine only at night. So it returns to what we have said. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿And from the evil of those who blow upon knots﴾. Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: this means the sorceresses. Mujahid said: when they perform incantations and blow into the knots.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: There is nothing closer to shirk than the incantation for snakebite and for madness.

And in another hadith: Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You have been unwell, O Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I recite over you, from every ailment that harms you, and from the evil of every envier and eye. May Allah cure you." [Sahih Muslim no. 2186, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Perhaps this was among his ailments, peace be upon him, when he was bewitched, then Allah the Exalted healed and cured him, and turned the plot of the envious sorcerers, the Jews, back upon their own heads, made their scheming return upon them, and exposed them. Yet despite this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never once reproached him for it. Rather, Allah sufficed, healed and restored him to health.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), and he complained of it for several days. Then Gabriel came to him and said: "A man from the Jews has bewitched you; he tied knots for you in such-and-such a well. So send someone to bring them out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who extracted them, brought them, and untied them. [Zayd said:] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose as if he had been released from a rope, and he never mentioned that to the Jewish man, nor did it appear in his face at all, until he died.

This was narrated by al-Nasa'i from Hannad, from Abu Mu'awiya Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Darir. [Musnad 4/367; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/112.]

Al-Bukhari said in the "Book of Medicine" of his Sahih: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: I heard Sufyan ibn Uyayna say: The first who narrated this to us was Ibn Jurayj, who said: The family of Urwa narrated to me, from Urwa. I asked Hisham about it, and he narrated to us from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bewitched, to the point that he would seem to go to his wives but would not really go to them. Sufyan said: This is the most severe form of sorcery, when it reaches that state. Then he said: "O Aisha, do you know that Allah has given me a ruling on what I asked Him about? Two men came to me; one sat at my head and the other at my feet. The one at my head said to the other: 'What is wrong with the man?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.' He asked: 'Who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam, a man from Banu Zurayq, an ally of the Jews, who was a hypocrite.' He asked: 'With what?' He said: 'With a comb and combings.' He asked: 'Where is it?' He said: 'In the spathe of a male date palm, under a stone, in the well of Dharwan.'" She said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the well until he extracted it, and said: "This is the well that was shown to me. Its water looks like the infusion of henna, and its palm trees are like the heads of devils." He said: Then he extracted it. I said: "Why did you not...?" meaning: did you not seek to spread it? He said: "As for Allah, He has cured me, and I dislike to stir up evil against any of the people." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5765.]

He also narrated it from the hadith of Isa ibn Yunus, Abu Damra Anas ibn Iyad, Abu Usama, and Yahya al-Qattan, and in it: "She said: until it seemed to him that he had done a thing when he had not done it." And in his narration: "So he ordered the well to be buried." Al-Bukhari also mentioned that Ibn Abi al-Zinad and al-Layth ibn Sa'd also narrated it from Hisham. [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 5863, 6391, 5766.]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama and Abdullah ibn Numayr. Ahmad narrated it from Affan, from Wuhayb, from Hisham, with the same. [Sahih Muslim no. 2189; Musnad 6/96.]

Imam Ahmad also narrated it through Ibrahim ibn Khalid, from Rabah, from Ma'mar, from Hisham, from his father, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained for six months, appearing to come to his wives but not coming to them. Then two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. One of them said to the other: "What is wrong with him?" The other said: "He has been bewitched." He asked: "Who bewitched him?" He said: "Labid ibn al-A'sam." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[Al-Musnad (6/63).]]

The Ustadh and exegete al-Tha'labi said in his Tafsir: Ibn 'Abbas and 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A boy from among the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Jews approached him and kept at him until he took the comb of the Prophet's ﷺ head and several teeth from his comb, and gave them to the Jews, and they cast a spell on him with them. The one who took charge of this was a man among them called Labid [[Addition from M and A.]] ibn A'sam. Then he put them in a well belonging to Banu Zurayq, called Dharwan. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, his head hair fell out, and he remained for six months appearing to go to his wives while not going to them, and he began to waste away without knowing what afflicted him. Then while he was sleeping, two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: "What is wrong with this man?" He said: "He is under the influence of a spell (tubba)." He asked: "And what is tubba?" He said: "He has been bewitched (suhira)." He asked: "Who bewitched him?" He said: "Labid ibn A'sam, the Jew." He asked: "With what did he bewitch him?" He said: "With a comb and combings." He asked: "And where is it?" He said: "In a sheath of a date-palm spathe, under a rā'ūfa in the well of Dharwan." Al-Juff is the skin of the date-palm spathe, and al-Rā'ūfa is a protruding rock at the bottom of the well on which the one drawing water stands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up alarmed and said: "O 'Aishah, did you not realise that Allah has informed me of my illness?" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Ali, al-Zubayr and 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and they drained the water of the well until it looked like the soaking water of henna. Then they lifted the rock and took out the sheath, and in it were the combings of his head and teeth from his comb, and in it was a cord tied with twelve knots, stuck with needles. So Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, and every time he recited a verse, a knot came undone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt relief when the last knot was undone, and he stood up as if he had been released from a tether. Jibril, peace be upon him, began saying: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from an envier and an evil eye; may Allah cure you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take out the wicked man and kill him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for me, Allah has cured me, and I dislike that evil should be stirred up among the people." [[Al-Kashf wal-Bayan of al-Tha'labi (fol. 194, Mahmudiyya edition).]]

He cited it thus without an isnad, and in it there is strangeness, and in some of it there is severe objectionability, while parts of it have supporting evidence from what has preceded. And Allah knows best.

**Tafsir of the Two Surahs of Seeking Refuge (al-Mu'awwidhatayn)**

They are both Madani (revealed in Medina).

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Asim ibn Bahdalah informed us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Ibn Mas'ud [was] [[Addition from the Musnad.]] not writing the two Mu'awwidhat in his mushaf?" He said: "I bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed me that Jibril, peace be upon him, said to him: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak (﴿Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi al-falaq﴾).' So I said it. He said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind (﴿Qul a'udhu bi-rabbi an-nas﴾).' So I said it." So we say what the Prophet ﷺ said. [[Al-Musnad (5/129).]]

Abu Bakr al-Humaydi also narrated it in his Musnad, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah and Asim ibn Bahdalah narrated to us, that they both heard Zirr ibn Hubaysh say: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b about the two Mu'awwidhat, and I said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud erases them from the mushaf." He said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'It was said to me: Say, so I said.'" So we say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. [[Musnad al-Humaydi (1/185).]]

Ahmad also said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Asim, from Zirr, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about the two Mu'awwidhat, and he said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about them, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said it to you. So say it.'" My father said: "Then the Prophet ﷺ said to us..." So we say [it]. [[Al-Musnad (5/129).]]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, 'Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, and Asim narrated to us from Zirr, who said: I asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b and said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, your brother Ibn Mas'ud says such and such." He said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said.'" So we say as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4977).]]

Al-Bukhari also narrated it, and al-Nasa'i, from Qutaybah, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Abdah and Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, with the same wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4976).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: al-Azraq ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, al-Salt ibn Bahram narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, who said: "'Abd Allah used to erase the two Mu'awwidhat from the mushaf and say: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was only commanded to seek refuge with them, and 'Abd Allah did not recite with them.'" [[Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, no. (2301), via Muhammad ibn Abi Ya'qub, from Hassan ibn Ibrahim, and al-Bazzar said: "No one among the Companions followed 'Abd Allah in this. It is authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ that he recited them in prayer, and we have affirmed them in the mushaf."]]

'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad also narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, who said: "'Abd Allah used to erase the two Mu'awwidhat from his mushafs and say: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'" [[In the original: "from 'Abd Allah." The text reads "'Abd al-Rahman".]] Al-A'mash said: Asim narrated to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked us about them, and he said: 'It was said to me, so I said.'" [[Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/129).]]

This is well known among many of the reciters and jurists: that Ibn Mas'ud did not write the two Mu'awwidhat in his mushaf. Perhaps he had not heard them from the Prophet ﷺ, and they had not reached him through mass transmission (tawatur). Then perhaps he later returned from that view to the position of the majority, for the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wrote them in the leading mushafs, and sent them to all the regions in that form. And to Allah belongs all praise and favour.

Muslim said in his Sahih: Qutaybah narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Have you not seen verses that were revealed tonight, the like of which has never been seen: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind'?" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (814).]]

Ahmad, Muslim also, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from 'Uqbah, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/144); Sahih Muslim, no. (814); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2902); Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/158).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Ibn Jabir narrated to us, from al-Qasim Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: "While I was leading the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the reins on one of those mountain paths, he said to me: 'O 'Uqbah, will you not ride?'" He said: "I was too modest to ride his mount, so he said: 'O 'Uqbah, will you not ride?'" He said: [Addition from the Musnad.] "I feared it might be disobedience. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dismounted, and I rode for a short while, then he rode. Then he said: 'O 'Uqbah, shall I not teach you two surahs, among the best two surahs that people have recited?'" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he taught me: "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak" and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind." Then the prayer was established, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went forward and recited them in it. Then he passed by me and said: "How did you find them, O 'Uqbah? Recite them whenever you sleep and whenever you rise." [[In the original: "O 'Uqab"; the marginal note reads "O 'Uqb". Addition from the Musnad.]]

Al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, both from Ibn Jabir, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/144); Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/253).]]

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Harith, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Uqbah, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252-253); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1462).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Yazid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Ru'ayni and Abu Marhum narrated to me, from Yazid ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from 'Ali ibn Rabah, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the Mu'awwidhat (al-mu'awwidhat) at the end of every prayer.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated it through several routes, from 'Ali ibn Abi Rabah. [[Al-Musnad (4/155); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1523); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2903); Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/68).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib."

Another route: Ahmad said: Yahya [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "Muhammad".]] ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Mashrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Recite the two Mu'awwidhat, for you will never recite the like of them." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (4/146).]]

Another route: Ahmad said: Haywah ibn Shurayh narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was presented with a white mule, and he mounted it, and 'Uqbah took its reins to lead it for him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Uqbah".]] said: "Recite: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.'" So he repeated it for him until he had recited it. He noticed that I was not very pleased with it, so he said: "Perhaps you were careless about it? For you have never stood in prayer reciting anything like it."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Baqiyyah, with the same wording. [[Al-Musnad (4/149); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, nos. (7843-7844).]] Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir: that he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the two Mu'awwidhat, and he related something similar. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la informed us, al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, I heard al-Nu'man, from Ziyad Abi al-Asad, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "People have never sought refuge with the like of these two: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7856).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Abu 'Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "O 'Uqbah, say." I said: "What shall I say?" He was silent with me, then he said: "Say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He was silent with me. So I said: "O Allah, return it to me." He said: "O 'Uqbah, say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,'" and I recited it until I reached its end. Then he said: "Say." I said: "What shall I say, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: 'I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind,'" and I recited it until I reached its end. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said at that point: "No one has asked with the like of these two, nor has anyone sought refuge with the like of these two." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/253).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Muhammad ibn Yasar informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Harith, from Makhul, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited them both in the Fajr prayer. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/252).]]

Another route: al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu 'Imran Aslam, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: I followed [[In the manuscript M: "I came to".]] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was riding, so I placed my hands on his foot [[In the manuscripts (M and A): "on his feet".]] and said: "Teach me Surah Hud or Surah Yusuf." He said: "You will not recite anything more beneficial [[In the manuscript M: "more effective".]] in the sight of Allah than: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.'" [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/254).]]

Another hadith: al-Nasa'i said: Mahmud ibn Khalid informed us, al-Walid narrated to us, Abu 'Amr al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'A'ish [[In the manuscript A: "Ibn 'Abbas".]] al-Juhani, that the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "O son of 'A'ish, shall I not show you, or inform you, of the best that those who seek refuge can seek refuge with?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind'; these are the two surahs." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/251).]]

Thus these routes from 'Uqbah are, as a body, like mutawatir reports from him, which give certainty according to many of the verifying scholars of hadith.

It has already been mentioned in the narration of Sudayy ibn 'Ajlan and Farwah ibn Mujahid, from him: "Shall I not teach you three surahs, the like of which has not been revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Furqan [[In the manuscript A: "in the Qur'an".]]? 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (﴿Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad﴾), 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'"

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Isma'il narrated to us, al-Juraydi narrated to us, from Abu al-'Ala', who said: A man said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and the people were taking turns riding, and the mounts on the back were few. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ's turn came, and then mine. He caught up with me and struck my shoulders [[Addition from the Musnad.]] and said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it, and I recited it with him. Then he said: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it, and I recited it with him. Then he said: 'When you pray, recite them both.'" [[Al-Musnad (5/24).]]

It appears that this man was 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and Allah knows best.

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, with the same wording. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (7859).]]

**Another hadith:** Al-Nasa'i said: Amr ibn Ali Abu Hafs informed us: Badal narrated to us: Shaddad ibn Sa'id Abu Talha narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, who narrated to us, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Recite, O Jabir." I said: "What should I recite, may my father and mother be your ransom?" He said: "Recite: 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak,' and 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind.'" So I recited them, and he said: "Recite with them, for you will never recite the like of them." [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 7854.]

**Another hadith:** Al-Nasa'i said: Amr ibn Ali Abu Hafs informed us... [as above chain].

The hadith of Aisha has already passed, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recite them (the two surahs) and blow into his palms, then wipe with them his head, his face, and whatever part of his body he could reach.

Imam Malik said: From Ibn Shihab, from Urwa, from Aisha: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever he was ill, would recite over himself the two Mu'awwidhatain (the two surahs of seeking refuge) and blow. When his pain grew severe, I would recite over him and wipe with his hand over him, seeking its blessing.

This was narrated by al-Bukhari from Abdullah ibn Yusuf, Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, al-Nasa'i from Qutayba and from the narrations of Ibn al-Qasim and Isa ibn Yunus, and Ibn Majah from the narrations of Ma'n and Bishr ibn Umar. All eight narrated it from Malik, with this wording. [Muwatta' 2/942; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5016; Sahih Muslim no. 3902; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 3902; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra nos. 7549, 7544, 10847; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 3529.]

It has already passed at the end of the surah "Nun" (Surah al-Qalam), from the hadith of Abu Nadra, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eye of jinn and humans. When the two Mu'awwidhatain were revealed, he took them and abandoned whatever else. This was narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi said: it is a hasan (sound-good) hadith.

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful**

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Isam narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us: Hasan ibn Salih narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: "al-falaq" is the dawn.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is the dawn. It was also narrated from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, al-Hasan, Qatada, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd, and Malik from Zayd ibn Aslam, the same as this.

Al-Qurazi, Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir said: it is like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿the Cleaver of the daybreak﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

Ali ibn Abi Talha said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is the creation. Likewise al-Dahhak said: Allah commanded His Prophet to seek refuge from all of creation.

Ka'b al-Ahbar (ka'b al-Ahbar) said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is a house in Hell; when it is opened, all the people of the Fire cry out because of its intense heat. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this, then said:

My father narrated to us: Suhayl ibn Uthman narrated to us, from a man he named, from al-Suddi, from Zayd ibn Ali, from his fathers, that they said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is a pit at the bottom of Hell, covered by a lid. When it is uncovered, a fire emerges from it, and Hell cries out because of the intense heat of what comes out of it.

Similarly it was narrated from Amr ibn Abasa and al-Suddi and others. A marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith has come on this, but it is munkar (rejected). Ibn Jarir said:

Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti narrated to me: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan al-Wasiti narrated to us: Nasr ibn Khuzayma al-Khurasani narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "al-Falaq is a covered pit in Hell." [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/225.] Its isnad is gharib (unusual), and its raising to the Prophet is not authentic.

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli said: ﴿al-Falaq﴾ is one of the names of Hell.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is the first, that it is the cleaving of the dawn. This is the sound view, and it is the choice of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, in his Sahih. [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/225; Sahih al-Bukhari 8/741, Fath.]

* *

His words: ﴿from the evil of what He created﴾ mean: from the evil of all created beings. Thabit al-Bunani and al-Hasan al-Basri said: Hell, Iblis and his offspring are among what He created.

﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾. Mujahid said: "al-ghasiq" is the night, "when it settles" means the setting of the sun. Al-Bukhari reported this from him, and Ibn Abi Najih narrated it from him. Likewise Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, Khusayf, al-Hasan and Qatada said: it is the night when it approaches with its darkness.

Al-Zuhri said: "when it settles" refers to the sun when it sets. From Atiyya and Qatada: "when the night settles" means when it departs. Abu al-Muhazzim, from Abu Hurayra, said: "al-ghasiq" is a star. Ibn Zayd said: the Arabs used to say that "al-ghasiq" is the setting of the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), and diseases and plagues would increase when it set, and would lift when it rose.

Ibn Jarir said: For these views there is a report that Nasr ibn Ali narrated to me: Bakkar ibn Abdullah, the nephew of Hammam, narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "﴿And from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾, he said: 'the star al-ghasiq.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari 30/227.]

I say: This hadith is not authentic in its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: it is the moon.

I say: The main evidence of the proponents of this view is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abu Dawud al-Hafari narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Harith, from Abu Salama, who said: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took my hand, showed me the moon as it rose, and said: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this darkness when it settles."

It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in the books of tafsir of their Sunan, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from his maternal uncle al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, with the same. al-Tirmidhi said: hasan sahih. The wording is: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, for this is the darkness when it settles." The wording of al-Nasa'i is: "Seek refuge in Allah from the evil of this, this is the darkness when it settles." [Musnad 6/61; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3366; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 10138.]

The proponents of the first view, that it is the night when it comes in, said: This does not contradict our view, because the moon is a sign of the night, its authority exists only in it, and likewise the stars shine only at night. So it returns to what we have said. And Allah knows best.

* *

His words: ﴿And from the evil of those who blow upon knots﴾. Mujahid, Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: this means the sorceresses. Mujahid said: when they perform incantations and blow into the knots.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, who said: There is nothing closer to shirk than the incantation for snakebite and for madness.

And in another hadith: Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "You have been unwell, O Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I recite over you, from every ailment that harms you, and from the evil of every envier and eye. May Allah cure you." [Sahih Muslim no. 2186, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Perhaps this was among his ailments, peace be upon him, when he was bewitched, then Allah the Exalted healed and cured him, and turned the plot of the envious sorcerers, the Jews, back upon their own heads, made their scheming return upon them, and exposed them. Yet despite this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never once reproached him for it. Rather, Allah sufficed, healed and restored him to health.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), and he complained of it for several days. Then Gabriel came to him and said: "A man from the Jews has bewitched you; he tied knots for you in such-and-such a well. So send someone to bring them out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who extracted them, brought them, and untied them. [Zayd said:] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose as if he had been released from a rope, and he never mentioned that to the Jewish man, nor did it appear in his face at all, until he died.

This was narrated by al-Nasa'i from Hannad, from Abu Mu'awiya Muhammad ibn Hazim al-Darir. [Musnad 4/367; Sunan al-Nasa'i 7/112.]

Al-Bukhari said in the "Book of Medicine" of his Sahih: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: I heard Sufyan ibn Uyayna say: The first who narrated this to us was Ibn Jurayj, who said: The family of Urwa narrated to me, from Urwa. I asked Hisham about it, and he narrated to us from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bewitched, to the point that he would seem to go to his wives but would not really go to them. Sufyan said: This is the most severe form of sorcery, when it reaches that state. Then he said: "O Aisha, do you know that Allah has given me a ruling on what I asked Him about? Two men came to me; one sat at my head and the other at my feet. The one at my head said to the other: 'What is wrong with the man?' The other said: 'He has been bewitched.' He asked: 'Who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam, a man from Banu Zurayq, an ally of the Jews, who was a hypocrite.' He asked: 'With what?' He said: 'With a comb and combings.' He asked: 'Where is it?' He said: 'In the spathe of a male date palm, under a stone, in the well of Dharwan.'" She said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) went to the well until he extracted it, and said: "This is the well that was shown to me. Its water looks like the infusion of henna, and its palm trees are like the heads of devils." He said: Then he extracted it. I said: "Why did you not...?" meaning: did you not seek to spread it? He said: "As for Allah, He has cured me, and I dislike to stir up evil against any of the people." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5765.]

He also narrated it from the hadith of Isa ibn Yunus, Abu Damra Anas ibn Iyad, Abu Usama, and Yahya al-Qattan, and in it: "She said: until it seemed to him that he had done a thing when he had not done it." And in his narration: "So he ordered the well to be buried." Al-Bukhari also mentioned that Ibn Abi al-Zinad and al-Layth ibn Sa'd also narrated it from Hisham. [Sahih al-Bukhari nos. 5863, 6391, 5766.]

Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Abu Usama Hammad ibn Usama and Abdullah ibn Numayr. Ahmad narrated it from Affan, from Wuhayb, from Hisham, with the same. [Sahih Muslim no. 2189; Musnad 6/96.]

Imam Ahmad also narrated it through Ibrahim ibn Khalid, from Rabah, from Ma'mar, from Hisham, from his father, from 'Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained for six months, appearing to come to his wives but not coming to them. Then two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. One of them said to the other: "What is wrong with him?" The other said: "He has been bewitched." He asked: "Who bewitched him?" He said: "Labid ibn al-A'sam." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[Al-Musnad (6/63).]]

The Ustadh and exegete al-Tha'labi said in his Tafsir: Ibn 'Abbas and 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A boy from among the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Jews approached him and kept at him until he took the comb of the Prophet's ﷺ head and several teeth from his comb, and gave them to the Jews, and they cast a spell on him with them. The one who took charge of this was a man among them called Labid [[Addition from M and A.]] ibn A'sam. Then he put them in a well belonging to Banu Zurayq, called Dharwan. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell ill, his head hair fell out, and he remained for six months appearing to go to his wives while not going to them, and he began to waste away without knowing what afflicted him. Then while he was sleeping, two angels came to him; one sat at his head and the other at his feet. The one at his feet said to the one at his head: "What is wrong with this man?" He said: "He is under the influence of a spell (tubba)." He asked: "And what is tubba?" He said: "He has been bewitched (suhira)." He asked: "Who bewitched him?" He said: "Labid ibn A'sam, the Jew." He asked: "With what did he bewitch him?" He said: "With a comb and combings." He asked: "And where is it?" He said: "In a sheath of a date-palm spathe, under a rā'ūfa in the well of Dharwan." Al-Juff is the skin of the date-palm spathe, and al-Rā'ūfa is a protruding rock at the bottom of the well on which the one drawing water stands. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ woke up alarmed and said: "O 'Aishah, did you not realise that Allah has informed me of my illness?" Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Ali, al-Zubayr and 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and they drained the water of the well until it looked like the soaking water of henna. Then they lifted the rock and took out the sheath, and in it were the combings of his head and teeth from his comb, and in it was a cord tied with twelve knots, stuck with needles. So Allah the Exalted sent down the two surahs, and every time he recited a verse, a knot came undone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ felt relief when the last knot was undone, and he stood up as if he had been released from a tether. Jibril, peace be upon him, began saying: "In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from an envier and an evil eye; may Allah cure you." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not take out the wicked man and kill him?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for me, Allah has cured me, and I dislike that evil should be stirred up among the people." [[Al-Kashf wal-Bayan of al-Tha'labi (fol. 194, Mahmudiyya edition).]]

He cited it thus without an isnad, and in it there is strangeness, and in some of it there is severe objectionability, while parts of it have supporting evidence from what has preceded. And Allah knows best.
